mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4% for three straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces revenue growth for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their prior 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > prior 12-month avg AND CPIAUCSL > prior 12-month avg
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their prior 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% month-over-month indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 3% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall by more than 3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average AND UNRATE stable (change < 0.1pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average and UNRATE is stable.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 forward returns exists over the next 5 trading days, as improving manufacturing activity rapidly boosts earnings expectations and market sentiment.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly INDPRO growth and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample testing.
